name: history-note-bounded-reads
goal: Read large Git note sets without collecting every blob in one batch while preserving each note and revision.

steps.title: Identify the failing behavior, expected behavior, and reproduction.
steps.evidence: Reading the preserved history loads 1,620 note blobs and 79,797 entries; the current all() requests every blob together and the isolated diagnostic observed 749,043,712 bytes process RSS after loading.

steps.title: Explain why existing standardized tests missed the bug; name the scenario, fixture, lifecycle or assertion gap and reusable test change.
steps.evidence: The existing notes-alone order case uses only two commits and does not constrain a large all() read. Extend that same case with a disposable many-note Git fixture and pinned-revision checks; do not add a test.

steps.title: Strengthen the existing standardized test; commit it before repair, run it failing with loop record --phase red, and preserve the assertion.
steps.evidence: Committed test b301644345; red record 3ffaf20f7a3c failed because one payload requested 130 blobs instead of at most 64.

steps.title: Implement the smallest repair without weakening the regression test.
steps.evidence: b7e48fe6ca parses at most 64 note blobs per Git payload while retaining original order and pinned revisions.

steps.title: Rerun the same unchanged regression test at a separate fix commit with loop record --phase green; preserve passing proof.
steps.evidence: Red 759a041a055f and green 56749ce13b8f used the identical command, tests, runtime and environment; the unchanged case passed at b7e48fe6ca.

steps.title: Run relevant project checks and affected UI browser flows with fresh inspected screenshots and no unexpected browser errors; preserve diagnostics and keep pending until proof passes.
